Title: Weather/temperature-sensitive vasomotor rhinitis may be refractory to intranasal corticosteroid treatment
Author: Jacobs, Lieberman, Kent, Silvey, Locantore, Philpot
Comment: Safety/AE data are reported only POOLED across the two replicate trials (FFR30006 + FFR30007); per-study epistaxis counts are not reported, so a single pooled row is recorded instead of two study-level rows. No significance test or effect measure is reported for epistaxis (descriptive counts only). Dose tested was 110 µg/day fluticasone furoate (single-dose trial), below the plan's 200–400 µg/day window, but no alternative dose arm exists.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fluticasone furoate nasal spray, 110 µg q.d.') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group RCT (two replicate trials, pooled)
Country: United States, Canada, Czech Republic, Germany, Norway, Romania
Participant type: Outpatients ≥12 years (US, Romania) or ≥18 years (Canada, Czech Republic, Germany, Norway) with ≥2-year history of perennial weather/temperature-triggered vasomotor (nonallergic) rhinitis
Recruitment source: 106 investigative centers in six countries, July 2005 to January 2006
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of subjects reporting epistaxis as an adverse event during the 4-week treatment period
effect_direction: More epistaxis with fluticasone furoate than placebo (16/353, 5% vs 9/346, 3%)

Report_ID: Epistaxis (nose bleeding) as reported side effect
Title: Reduction of Metacholine-Induced Nasal Secretion by Treatment with a New Topical Steroid in Perennial Non-Allergic Rhinitis
Author: Malm, Wihl, Lamm & Lindqvist
Comment: Cross-over design: the same 22 patients received both placebo and budesonide, so arms are not independent; totals of 22 per arm are period-level. No inferential statistic reported for side effects. Events counted from narrative text only.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Budesonide 200 µg/day intranasal aerosol') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adult patients with perennial non-allergic rhinitis (20-68 years, mean 42)
Recruitment source: Department of Otolaryngology, Malmö General Hospital
Outcome measurement: Number of patients reporting nose bleeding out of 22 patients per treatment period
Outcome variable: Epistaxis (nose bleeding) as reported side effect
effect_direction: More epistaxis with budesonide 200 µg/day than placebo (1/22 vs 0/22)

Report_ID: Epistaxis (number of patients reporting epistaxis as an adverse event)
Title: Mometasone Furoate Nasal Spray in the Treatment of Perennial Non-allergic Rhinitis: A Nordic, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study
Author: Lundblad, Sipilä, Farstad, Drozdziewicz
Comment: Arm denominators for the adverse-event tabulation are not stated verbatim; they are implied by the reported percentages (21/169 = 12.4%; 9/162 = 5.6%). Efficacy ITT tables list MFNS n=167 and placebo n=162. No test statistic or p-value is reported for the epistaxis comparison ("no significant difference" stated narratively only).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Mometasone furoate nasal spray (MFNS) 200 µg once daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Content length: 6 weeks double-blind treatment plus 3 weeks follow-up
Participant type: adults aged 18–82 years with perennial non-allergic rhinitis (mean duration 9 years)
Recruitment source: 16 clinical sites (7 Sweden, 3 Denmark, 3 Finland, 3 Norway)
Outcome measurement: Count and percentage of patients with epistaxis reported as an adverse event per treatment arm
Outcome variable: Epistaxis (number of patients reporting epistaxis as an adverse event)
effect_direction: More epistaxis with mometasone furoate 200 µg/day than placebo (21/169, 12.4% vs 9/162, 5.6%)

Report_ID: Epistaxis (nosebleed) incidence as an adverse event
Title: Efficacy and Safety of Once Daily Fluticasone Furoate Nasal Spray for Treatment of Irritant (Non-allergic) Rhinitis
Author: Tantilipikorn et al.
Comment: The paper reports epistaxis only as percentages (4% FFNS vs 0 placebo); no explicit event counts are given. group_1_events=2 was derived as 4% of the FFNS N=53 (2.12 → 2 subjects) and is therefore an approximation, not verbatim; group_2_events=0 follows directly from the explicitly reported "0" for placebo. Denominators are the randomized/treated Ns (53 and 49; all randomized subjects received at least one dose). No statistical test, p-value, CI or effect size was reported for this or any adverse event; the trial was explicitly not powered for treatment comparisons.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fluticasone furoate nasal spray (FFNS) 110 mcg once daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter Phase IIa pilot RCT
Content length: 4-week treatment period with 3-5 day follow-up telephone call
Participant type: Subjects aged ≥12 years (range 12-64) with irritant (non-allergic) rhinitis predominantly triggered by air pollution
Recruitment source: 7 study centers in Thailand (March 2008 – February 2009); FFR111158, NCT00730756
Outcome measurement: Percent of subjects reporting epistaxis as an adverse event (FFNS 4% vs placebo 0)
Outcome variable: Epistaxis (nosebleed) incidence as an adverse event
effect_direction: More epistaxis with fluticasone furoate than placebo (4% vs 0%; ~2/53 vs 0/49)
